blocks.text: DAT:100–122 DETAILED REVIEW AND DELEGATED APPROVAL — CANONICAL

The Data process block was reconsidered from first principles under the standing delegated authority. The review compared five genuinely different architectures per root, scored 45 candidates across 360 criterion values, routed 133 English concepts without forced atomization, passed all 18 canonical packet checks, passed all 27 combined Data entity/process soundness checks, and passed the complete authority regression. All deterministic generated forms remained unchanged.

Approved architecture: DAT:1xx names substrate-neutral processes affecting represented information. The inward triplet transforms information while it remains within one reference entity; the outward triplet transfers bounded information from one source context to one distinct target; and the systemic triplet coordinates information-state alignment across multiple participants under one shared synchronization criterion. The third trit changes only completed, active, or nonactualized phase.

DAT:100 — completed internal data transformation — Completion of a bounded transformation of represented information within one reference entity, yielding transformed information without transferring it to a distinct target.

DAT:101 — active internal data transformation — An ongoing bounded transformation of represented information within one reference entity that is producing transformed information without transferring it to a distinct target.

DAT:102 — nonactualized internal data transformation — A nonactualized bounded transformation that would transform represented information within one reference entity without transferring it to a distinct target.

DAT:110 — completed target data transfer — Completion of a bounded information transfer from one source context to one distinct reference target, causing that target to receive the transferred information.

DAT:111 — active target data transfer — An ongoing bounded information transfer from one source context to one distinct reference target that is causing that target to receive the transferred information.
DAT:112 — nonactualized target data transfer — A nonactualized bounded information transfer that would carry information from one source context to one distinct reference target.
DAT:120 — completed systemic data synchronization — Completion of a coordinated information-state alignment across multiple participants in one shared data domain under one synchronization criterion.
DAT:121 — active systemic data synchronization — An ongoing coordinated information-state alignment across multiple participants in one shared data domain under one synchronization criterion.

DAT:122 — nonactualized systemic data synchronization — A nonactualized coordinated process that would align information states across multiple participants in one shared data domain under one synchronization criterion.

Design boundary: these roots do not silently encode the information entity itself; physical signal, carrier, storage medium, energy, or spatial displacement; communicative intent, sender/addressee role, channel, uptake, or acknowledgment; cognition, observation, belief, or understanding; formal evaluation; novel-content creation; restoration; a specific codec, algorithm, schema, merge policy, fidelity, integrity result, persistence, access, scheduling, probability, or modality. Completed processing does not entail external success conditions. Lexical third-trit 2 remains nonactualized only and is distinct from runtime [2]/num uncertainty.
